summary: The note describes the Argus Fernfeuer, a concept for an aircraft-sized unmanned aerial vehicle that grew out of the Argus As 292 project and was also designed by Fritz Gosslau. Gosslau proposed it during testing of the smaller As 292 drone, envisioning a craft that could deliver a one-tonne drop charge over long distances. It would be controlled by line-of-sight radio or radio beam, and a manned aircraft outside local defenses would signal it to release its load before the Fernfeuer returned to base.
one_line: The Argus Fernfeuer was a proposed aircraft-sized UAV, designed by Fritz Gosslau from the Argus As 292 project, to deliver a one-tonne drop charge over long distances.
key_facts: The Argus Fernfeuer arose from the Argus As 292 project.
The Argus Fernfeuer was designed by Fritz Gosslau.
Fritz Gosslau proposed the Argus Fernfeuer during testing of the small As 292 drone.
The Argus Fernfeuer was conceived as an aircraft-sized UAV.
The Argus Fernfeuer was intended to deliver a one tonne drop charge over long distances.
The Argus Fernfeuer could be controlled by line-of-sight radio control.
The Argus Fernfeuer could alternatively be controlled by radio beam direction.
A manned aircraft flying clear of local defenses would signal the Argus Fernfeuer to release the drop-load.
After releasing its drop-load, the Argus Fernfeuer would return to base.
